title: Dense Apple Cider Donuts
description: Baked cake donuts flavored with reduced cider, dipped in spiced sugar.
beforeYouStart: Reduce the cider at least 30 minutes ahead, or the night before, so it has time to cool.
Egg and milk at room temperature.
Preheat to 350F and coat the donut pan with nonstick spray.
Two donut pans let you bake everything at once; with one, bake in batches.

items.do: Simmer the cider in a small saucepan over low heat, stirring now and then. Start measuring at 10 minutes, then every 3 to 5 minutes. Leave any spices or solids that rise to the top; they go into the batter too.
items.cue: Down to 1/2 cup (120 ml), thick and concentrated

items.do: Take off the heat and let it cool before it goes into the batter.
Whisk the flour, baking soda, baking powder, cinnamon, apple pie spice and salt in a large bowl.

In a second bowl, whisk the melted butter, egg, both sugars, milk and vanilla. Pour into the dry ingredients, add the cooled cider reduction, and whisk until smooth. The batter should be a little thick; that's what makes the crumb dense and cakey.
Scrape the batter into a large zip-top bag, snip off a corner, and pipe into the pan, filling each cavity about halfway.

items.cue: Edges and tops lightly browned; the top springs back when poked

items.do: Cool in the pan, then turn out onto a wire rack. Re-grease the pan and bake the remaining batter.
Stir the sugar, cinnamon and apple pie spice together in a medium bowl.

Once the donuts are cool enough to handle, dip both sides quickly in the melted butter, then coat generously in the spiced sugar. Don't let them soak: they drink butter fast, and if the bowl runs low, brush it on instead.

items: Best the day they're made. Keeps covered at room temperature up to 2 days, or in the fridge up to 5 days.
Freeze, coated or plain, up to 2 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge and rewarm in the microwave.
The cider reduction can be made the night before. The batter can't: the leaveners start working once wet meets dry, so bake soon after mixing.
Apple pie spice: mix 4 parts cinnamon, 2 parts nutmeg and 1 part cardamom.
Milk: the author usually uses buttermilk, but any dairy or nondairy milk works. 1/2 cup plain yogurt or sour cream gives a denser crumb.

No donut pan: use a greased or lined 12-cup muffin pan, fill each cup 3/4 full, and bake at 350F for 18 to 20 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Makes 10 to 12. With more cake and less coating per bite, they eat more like a muffin; the minis below come closest to a donut.
Minis: grease a mini donut or mini muffin pan, fill 3/4 full, and bake at 350F for 8 to 9 minutes.
